title: Construction-Dependent Floquet Topology in Circularly Driven $N$-Stacked Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chains
abstract: We investigate construction-dependent Floquet topology in a two-dimensional lattice formed by stacking Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chains with co-located sublattice orbitals. We present two constructions in the decoupled-chain limit. Construction-I: the constituent SSH chains are topologically trivial with winding number $w=0$. Construction-II: the constituent SSH chains are topologically nontrivial with $w=1$. Although these constructions are unitarily equivalent in the static limit, circular driving distinguishes them because the hopping processes related by the transformation correspond to different physical bond vectors and therefore acquire different Peierls phases. Using the Floquet-Sambe formalism, we determine the quasienergy spectra and phase diagrams in terms of the lower-band Chern number $C_L$ and directional Zak phases $(Z_x,\, Z_y)$. We find distinct Floquet phase structures, including low-frequency phases with $C_L = -3$ and $C_L = -4$ in the two constructions. Since the Chern number does not resolve the topology of the two quasienergy gaps separately, we further calculate the dynamical winding numbers $W_0$ and $W_π$, and verify the corresponding chiral edge states. In particular, at identical driving parameters, both constructions can have the same Chern numbers $C_L=-2$, while their gap-resolved winding numbers are $(W_0,\, W_π)=(0,\,+2)$ and $(-2,\,0)$, respectively. We also calculate the time-averaged optical Hall conductivity and show that $ C_Le^2/h$ determines its dc value for ideal full-band occupation. At the same time, its finite-frequency response contains photon-assisted contributions. Our results demonstrate that the physical construction of the constituent chains, although irrelevant to the static bulk spectrum, can play a decisive role in the Floquet topological structure. We discuss possible experimental realizations of the driven model.
summary: This paper explores the construction-dependent Floquet topology in stacked SSH chains driven by circular light. By comparing two physically distinct constructions, the authors show that while the static bulk spectrum might be identical, the time-periodic driving reveals different topological signatures via dynamical winding numbers. This highlights that the physical realization of the lattice structure is crucial for understanding driven topological matter.
main_problem: The study investigates how the physical construction of constituent chains affects the Floquet topological properties of a 2D lattice formed by stacking Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chains under circular driving.
main_result: The physical construction dictates distinct Floquet topological structures, evidenced by different gap-resolved winding numbers $(W_0, W_\pi)$, even when the static bulk Chern number ($C_L$) remains the same.
method: The analysis employs the Floquet-Sambe formalism to determine quasienergy spectra and topological invariants, including the Chern number and dynamical winding numbers.
model_or_system: The system is an N-stacked SSH chain model subjected to a time-periodic Hamiltonian induced by circular driving, analyzed in the decoupled-chain limit.
key_observables: Lower-band Chern number ($C_L$), directional Zak phases ($Z_x, Z_y$), and dynamical winding numbers ($W_0, W_\pi$).
important_parameters: Driving frequency ($\Omega$), dimerization ($\eta$), and interchain hopping ($\delta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system is in the time-periodic regime and focuses on the $\chi = -1$ driving case.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Floquet phase diagrams, showing how different constructions yield distinct topological invariants like $(W_0, W_\pi)$ for the same $C_L$.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the driven Hamiltonian and then uses the Floquet-Sambe formalism to calculate topological invariants. It compares two distinct constructions (I and II) to demonstrate the construction dependence, culminating in the calculation of gap-resolved winding numbers.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it demonstrates that subtle details of the physical realization (the 'construction') can dictate the topological properties of a driven system, going beyond what is captured by static invariants like the Chern number.
